entities.summary: Tiberius Julius Sauromates II Philocaesar Philoromaios Eusebes, also known as Sauromates II, was a Roman client king of the Bosporan Kingdom, ruling from 172–210 CE. He was the son of Sauromates I and succeeded his father as king of the Bosporan Kingdom. His reign is documented through his coins, which are known from the period 172–210, likely accounting for his entire rule. Sauromates II's reign is notable for its significance in the history of the Bosporan Kingdom, which was a key player in the Roman Empire's eastern provinces. The king's ability to maintain his kingdom's independence and navigate the complex web of Roman client states is a testament to his skill as a ruler. Despite being a client king, Sauromates II was able to maintain a degree of autonomy and make decisions that benefited his kingdom. His reign also saw the rise of the Roman Empire's power in the region, which would have significant consequences for the future of the Bosporan Kingdom. The legacy of Sauromates II can be seen in the continued existence of the Bosporan Kingdom until its eventual absorption into the Roman Empire in the 4th century CE. He is remembered as one of the most significant figures in the history of the Bosporan Kingdom, marking a period of relative stability and prosperity for the kingdom.
